function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content: I’m sorry—I don’t have direct access to your device’s clock or a way to fetch the exact current time right now. If you let me know which time zone (or city) you’re interested in, I can give you the standard time difference from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), so you can calculate the local time yourself.

The user asks "What time is it?" This requires providing the current local time. There's no tool for getting system time; we can use built-in knowledge or approximate. We should respond with an apology about not having real-time capability but provide best guess based on UTC offset maybe. But better to say I don't have access to live clock.

We could also ask clarifying question like what timezone they want. Let's answer politely.
